title: NEET (UG) 2022 · 17 July 2022 · Code Q1
instr: NEET (UG) 2022 held on 17 July 2022, Test Booklet Code Q1, with the final answer key published by the National Testing Agency (NTA) on 7 September 2022.

200 questions: Physics 1–50, Chemistry 51–100, Botany 101–150, Zoology 151–200. Each subject has Section A (35 compulsory questions) and Section B (15 questions, of which candidates had to attempt any 10). Each question has four options (1)–(4) with one correct answer.

Marking: +4 for a correct answer, −1 for a wrong answer, 0 if not answered. As in the exam, only the first 10 questions you answer in each Section B are marked, so the maximum is 720 marks (180 questions).
Q93 (Chemistry) was dropped by NTA, so everyone gets its 4 marks.
source: Questions: NEET (UG) 2022, Test Booklet Code Q1. Answers: NTA final answer key published on 7 September 2022. Explanations: All in All Exam Practice.

questions.text: An ideal gas undergoes four different processes from the same initial state as shown in the figure below. Those processes are adiabatic, isothermal, isobaric and isochoric. The curve which represents the adiabatic process among 1, 2, 3 and 4 is
questions.sol:
Curve 4 (constant $P$) is isobaric and curve 1 (constant $V$) is isochoric.
Of the two falling curves, the adiabatic is steeper than the isothermal, because its slope is $-\gamma P/V$ against $-P/V$. Curve 2 falls more steeply, so it is the adiabatic.

questions.text: The angular speed of a fly wheel moving with uniform angular acceleration changes from 1200 rpm to 3120 rpm in 16 seconds. The angular acceleration in rad/s$^2$ is
questions.sol:
$\omega_1 = \dfrac{1200 \times 2\pi}{60} = 40\pi$ rad/s and $\omega_2 = \dfrac{3120 \times 2\pi}{60} = 104\pi$ rad/s.
$\alpha = \dfrac{104\pi - 40\pi}{16} = 4\pi$ rad/s$^2$.

questions.text: In the given circuits (a), (b) and (c), the potential drop across the two $p$-$n$ junctions are equal in
questions.sol:
In (a) and (c) the two diodes face the same way in the series loop, so both are forward biased (or both reverse biased) and they carry the same current: identical diodes then have equal potential drops.
In (b) the diodes face opposite ways, so one is forward biased and the other reverse biased; almost all of the battery voltage appears across the reverse-biased one.

questions.text: A biconvex lens has radii of curvature, 20 cm each. If the refractive index of the material of the lens is 1.5, the power of the lens is
questions.sol:
Lens maker's formula: $\dfrac{1}{f} = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right) = 0.5\left(\dfrac{1}{0.2} + \dfrac{1}{0.2}\right) = 5\ \text{m}^{-1}$.
Power $= +5$ D.

questions.text: As the temperature increases, the electrical resistance
options: Increases for both conductors and semiconductors
Decreases for both conductors and semiconductors
Increases for conductors but decreases for semiconductors
Decreases for conductors but increases for semiconductors
questions.sol:
In a metal, the electrons collide more often with the vibrating ions as the temperature rises, so resistance increases.
In a semiconductor, more charge carriers are released as the temperature rises, so resistance decreases.

questions.text: If the initial tension on a stretched string is doubled, then the ratio of the initial and final speeds of a transverse wave along the string is
questions.sol:
$v = \sqrt{T/\mu}$, so $v \propto \sqrt{T}$.
$\dfrac{v_1}{v_2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{T}{2T}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$, i.e. $1 : \sqrt{2}$.

questions.text: A shell of mass $m$ is at rest initially. It explodes into three fragments having mass in the ratio 2 : 2 : 1. If the fragments having equal mass fly off along mutually perpendicular directions with speed $v$, the speed of the third (lighter) fragment is
questions.sol:
The masses are $\frac{2m}{5}, \frac{2m}{5}, \frac{m}{5}$. The two equal momenta $\frac{2m}{5}v$ are perpendicular, so their resultant is $\frac{2m}{5}v\sqrt{2}$.
Total momentum stays zero, so $\frac{m}{5}v' = \frac{2\sqrt{2}\,m}{5}v$, giving $v' = 2\sqrt{2}\,v$.

questions.text: If a soap bubble expands, the pressure inside the bubble
options: Is equal to the atmospheric pressure
questions.sol: The excess pressure inside a soap bubble is $\Delta P = 4S/R$. As the bubble expands, $R$ increases, so the excess pressure (and hence the pressure inside) decreases.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: An electric lift with a maximum load of 2000 kg (lift + passengers) is moving up with a constant speed of 1.5 ms$^{-1}$. The frictional force opposing the motion is 3000 N. The minimum power delivered by the motor to the lift in watts is : ($g$ = 10 ms$^{-2}$)
questions.sol:
At constant speed the motor must balance the weight and friction: $F = 2000 \times 10 + 3000 = 23000$ N.
$P = Fv = 23000 \times 1.5 = 34500$ W.

questions.text: The angle between the electric lines of force and the equipotential surface is
questions.sol: No work is done in moving a charge along an equipotential surface, so the field has no component along it: field lines always cross equipotential surfaces at 90°.

questions.text: When two monochromatic lights of frequency, $\nu$ and $\dfrac{\nu}{2}$ are incident on a photoelectric metal, their stopping potential becomes $\dfrac{V_s}{2}$ and $V_s$ respectively. The threshold frequency for this metal is
questions.sol:
Einstein's equation $eV = h u - h u_0$ for each light:
$\dfrac{eV_s}{2} = h u - h u_0$ and $eV_s = \dfrac{h u}{2} - h u_0$.
Doubling the first and equating: $2h u - 2h u_0 = \dfrac{h u}{2} - h u_0$, so $ u_0 = \dfrac{3}{2} u$.
(This is the formal result. Physically the data are inconsistent: a threshold above both frequencies would mean no emission at all.)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.note: The data in this question are not physically consistent: the lower frequency is given the larger stopping potential, and the result $\nu_0 = \frac{3}{2}\nu$ is above both frequencies used. NTA's final key keeps option (4), the value obtained by solving the two equations formally.

$B = \mu_0 n I = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 10^5 \times 1 = 12.56 \times 10^{-2}$ T. (The radius does not matter for a long solenoid.)

questions.text:
Given below are two statements
$\textbf{Statement I :}$ Biot-Savart's law gives us the expression for the magnetic field strength of an infinitesimal current element (Idl) of a current carrying conductor only.
$\textbf{Statement II :}$ Biot-Savart's law is analogous to Coulomb's inverse square law of charge $q$, with the former being related to the field produced by a scalar source, Idl while the latter being produced by a vector source, $q$.
In light of above statements choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct and Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect and Statement II is correct
questions.sol:
Statement I is correct: the Biot-Savart law gives the field $d\vec{B}$ due to a current element $I\,d\vec{l}$.
Statement II is incorrect: it has the sources the wrong way round. $I\,d\vec{l}$ is a vector source, while the charge $q$ in Coulomb's law is a scalar source.

questions.text: The ratio of the radius of gyration of a thin uniform disc about an axis passing through its centre and normal to its plane to the radius of gyration of the disc about its diameter is
questions.sol:
About the central normal axis $I = \frac{1}{2}MR^2$, so $k_1 = R/\sqrt{2}$. About a diameter $I = \frac{1}{4}MR^2$, so $k_2 = R/2$.
$k_1 : k_2 = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} : \dfrac{1}{2} = \sqrt{2} : 1$.

questions.text: In a Young's double slit experiment, a student observes 8 fringes in a certain segment of screen when a monochromatic light of 600 nm wavelength is used. If the wavelength of light is changed to 400 nm, then the number of fringes he would observe in the same region of the screen is
questions.sol:
Fringe width $\beta = \lambda D/d$, so the number of fringes in a fixed length is inversely proportional to $\lambda$.
$n_2 = 8 \times \dfrac{600}{400} = 12$.

questions.sol: The field is along the normal to the loop, so $\Phi = BA = 0.5 \times 1^2 = 0.5$ Wb. The resistance is not needed.

questions.text: Two resistors of resistance, 100 $\Omega$ and 200 $\Omega$ are connected in parallel in an electrical circuit. The ratio of the thermal energy developed in 100 $\Omega$ to that in 200 $\Omega$ in a given time is
questions.sol:
In parallel both have the same voltage, so heat $H = \dfrac{V^2t}{R} \propto \dfrac{1}{R}$.
$H_{100} : H_{200} = 200 : 100 = 2 : 1$.

questions.sol: From rest, distance in the $n$th second is $s_n = \frac{g}{2}(2n - 1)$, so the ratio is 1 : 3 : 5 : 7.

questions.text: A light ray falls on a glass surface of refractive index $\sqrt{3}$, at an angle 60°. The angle between the refracted and reflected rays would be
questions.sol:
Snell's law: $\sin r = \dfrac{\sin 60°}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$, so $r = 30°$.
The reflected ray makes 60° with the normal, so the angle between the reflected and refracted rays is $180° - 60° - 30° = 90°$. (Here $\tan 60° = \sqrt{3}$, so 60° is the Brewster angle.)
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: When light propagates through a material medium of relative permittivity $\varepsilon_r$ and relative permeability $\mu_r$, the velocity of light, $v$ is given by ($c$-velocity of light in vacuum)
questions.sol: $v = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu\varepsilon}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0\varepsilon_0}} \cdot \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_r\varepsilon_r}} = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\varepsilon_r\mu_r}}$.

questions.sol:

questions.text: Two pendulums of length 121 cm and 100 cm start vibrating in phase. At some instant, the two are at their mean position in the same phase. The minimum number of vibrations of the shorter pendulum after which the two are again in phase at the mean position is:
questions.sol:
$T \propto \sqrt{l}$, so $T_{long} : T_{short} = 11 : 10$.
They are next in phase when $n\,T_{short} = (n - 1)\,T_{long}$, i.e. $10n = 11(n - 1)$, so $n = 11$ vibrations of the shorter pendulum (10 of the longer).

questions.sol:

questions.sol: At the highest point only the horizontal component remains. At 60° to the vertical, it is $10 \sin 60° = 5\sqrt{3}$ m s$^{-1}$.

questions.text: The truth table for the given logic circuit is
questions.sol:
The upper NAND gate gets $A$ and $B$; the lower NAND gate gets $\overline{A}$ (through the NOT gate) and $B$. Their outputs feed an AND gate:
$C = \overline{AB}\cdot\overline{\overline{A}B}$.
$A, B = 0, 0$: $1 \cdot 1 = 1$; $0, 1$: $1 \cdot 0 = 0$; $1, 0$: $1 \cdot 1 = 1$; $1, 1$: $0 \cdot 1 = 0$.
$C = \overline{B}$, which is truth table (3).

questions.text: From Ampere's circuital law for a long straight wire of circular cross-section carrying a steady current, the variation of magnetic field in the inside and outside region of the wire is
options: Uniform and remains constant for both the regions.
A linearly increasing function of distance upto the boundary of the wire and then linearly decreasing for the outside region.
A linearly increasing function of distance $r$ upto the boundary of the wire and then decreasing one with $\dfrac{1}{r}$ dependence for the outside region.
A linearly decreasing function of distance upto the boundary of the wire and then a linearly increasing one for the outside region.
questions.sol:
Inside (uniform current): $B \cdot 2\pi r = \mu_0 I \dfrac{r^2}{R^2}$, so $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I r}{2\pi R^2} \propto r$.
Outside: $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r} \propto \dfrac{1}{r}$.

questions.text: A series LCR circuit with inductance 10 H, capacitance 10 $\mu$F, resistance 50 $\Omega$ is connected to an ac source of voltage, $V$ = 200sin(100$t$) volt. If the resonant frequency of the LCR circuit is $\nu_1$ and the frequency of the ac source is $\nu$, then
questions.sol:
$\omega_0 = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{LC}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{10 imes 10 imes 10^{-6}}} = 100$ rad/s, so $ u_0 = \dfrac{100}{2\pi} = \dfrac{50}{\pi}$ Hz.
The source has $\omega = 100$ rad/s, so $ u = \dfrac{50}{\pi}$ Hz as well. (The stem calls the resonant frequency $ u_1$; the options call it $ u_0$.)

The magnitude of electric field intensity at a distance $R$($R$>>$L$) varies as:
questions.sol: The pair is an electric dipole of moment $p = qL$. Far from a dipole ($R \gg L$), the field is proportional to $p/R^3$.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : One is labelled as $\textbf{Assertion (A)}$ and the other is labelled as $\textbf{Reason (R)}$.
$\textbf{Assertion (A):}$ The stretching of a spring is determined by the shear modulus of the material of the spring.
$\textbf{Reason (R):}$ A coil spring of copper has more tensile strength than a steel spring of same dimensions.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{most appropriate}$ answer from the options given below
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.sol:
(A) is true: when a coil spring is stretched, the wire is twisted rather than lengthened, so the change in shape depends on the shear modulus.
(R) is false: steel is stronger and more elastic than copper, so a steel spring has the greater tensile strength.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A big circular coil of 1000 turns and average radius 10 m is rotating about its horizontal diameter at 2 rad s$^{-1}$. If the vertical component of earth's magnetic field at that place is $2 \times 10^{-5}$ T and electrical resistance of the coil is 12.56 $\Omega$, then the maximum induced current in the coil will be
questions.sol:
Rotation about a horizontal diameter cuts the vertical component of the field.
$\varepsilon_{max} = NBA\omega = 1000 \times 2 \times 10^{-5} \times \pi (10)^2 \times 2 = 4\pi \approx 12.56$ V.
$I_{max} = 12.56/12.56 = 1$ A.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The volume occupied by the molecules contained in 4.5 kg water at STP, if the intermolecular forces vanish away is
questions.sol:
With no intermolecular forces the water behaves as an ideal gas.
Moles $= 4500/18 = 250$; at STP one mole occupies 22.4 L.
$V = 250 \times 22.4 = 5600$ L $= 5.6$ m$^3$.

questions.text: A capacitor of capacitance $C$ = 900 pF is charged fully by 100 V battery $B$ as shown in figure (a). Then it is disconnected from the battery and connected to another uncharged capacitor of capacitance $C$ = 900 pF as shown in figure (b). The electrostatic energy stored by the system (b) is
questions.sol:
Charge $Q = CV = 900 \times 10^{-12} \times 100 = 9 \times 10^{-8}$ C. Shared between two equal capacitors, the common potential is 50 V.
Energy $= 2 \times \frac{1}{2} \times 900 \times 10^{-12} \times 50^2 = 2.25 \times 10^{-6}$ J (half the original $4.5 \times 10^{-6}$ J).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A wheatstone bridge is used to determine the value of unknown resistance $X$ by adjusting the variable resistance $Y$ as shown in the figure. For the most precise measurement of $X$, the resistances $P$ and $Q$
options: should be approximately equal and are small
should be very large and unequal
do not play any significant role
questions.sol: A Wheatstone bridge is most sensitive when its four arms are of comparable value. With P and Q roughly equal and small, the galvanometer responds well to a small imbalance, so X can be found most precisely.

questions.text: Two transparent media $A$ and $B$ are separated by a plane boundary. The speed of light in those media are $1.5 \times 10^{8}$ m/s and $2.0 \times 10^{8}$ m/s, respectively. The critical angle for a ray of light for these two media is
questions.sol:
Light is slower in $A$, so $A$ is the denser medium. Total internal reflection happens for light going from $A$ to $B$.
$\sin C = \dfrac{n_B}{n_A} = \dfrac{v_A}{v_B} = \dfrac{1.5}{2.0} = 0.750$, so $C = \sin^{-1}(0.750)$.

questions.sol:
Work done is the area under the $p$-$V$ curve. Graph (2) shows an expansion over a wide range of volume, starting with a high constant pressure, and has the largest area under it.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as $\textbf{Assertion (A)}$ and the other is labelled as $\textbf{Reason (R)}$.
$\textbf{Assertion (A):}$ ICl is more reactive than I$_2$.
$\textbf{Reason (R):}$ I-Cl bond is weaker than I-I bond.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most $\textbf{appropriate}$ answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.sol: Interhalogen compounds are generally more reactive than the halogens (except fluorine), because the bond between two different halogens (X-X′) is weaker than the X-X bond. So both statements are correct and (R) explains (A), as NCERT states.

questions.text: Which compound amongst the following is $\textbf{not}$ an aromatic compound?
questions.sol:
Hückel's rule needs a planar, fully conjugated ring with $(4n + 2)\ \pi$ electrons.
(1) cyclopentadienyl anion: 6 $\pi$ e$^-$, aromatic. (2) tropylium (cycloheptatrienyl) cation: 6 $\pi$ e$^-$, aromatic. (3) cyclopropenyl cation: 2 $\pi$ e$^-$, aromatic.
(4) cycloheptatriene has an sp$^3$ CH$_2$ carbon, so the ring is not fully conjugated: it is not aromatic.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as $\textbf{Assertion (A)}$ and the other is labelled as $\textbf{Reason (R)}$.
$\textbf{Assertion (A):}$
In a particular point defect, an ionic solid is electrically neutral, even if few of its cations are missing from its unit cells.
$\textbf{Reason (R):}$
In an ionic solid, Frenkel defect arises due to dislocation of cation from its lattice site to interstitial site, maintaining overall electrical neutrality.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.sol:
(A) is correct: in a Schottky defect cations go missing together with an equal number of anions, and in a Frenkel defect the cation is only displaced. Either way the crystal stays neutral.
(R) is a correct description of the Frenkel defect, but no cation is missing from the crystal in that defect, so (R) does not explain (A).

questions.text: Which one is not correct mathematical equation for Dalton’s Law of partial pressure? Here p = total pressure of gaseous mixture
options:
p$_i$ = $\chi_i$p, where p$_i$ = partial pressure of i$^{\text{th}}$ gas
$\chi_i$ = mole fraction of i$^{\text{th}}$ gas in gaseous mixture

$\text{p}_i = \chi_i\text{p}_i^\circ$, where $\chi_i$ = mole fraction of i$^{\text{th}}$ gas in gaseous mixture
$\text{p}_i^\circ$ = pressure of i$^{\text{th}}$ gas in pure state
questions.sol:
(1), (2) and (3) are forms of Dalton's law: the total pressure is the sum of the partial pressures, each $p_i = n_iRT/V = \chi_i p$.
(4), $p_i = \chi_i p_i^\circ$, is Raoult's law for the vapour pressure of a component of a solution, not Dalton's law.

$\textbf{Statement I:}$

questions.text:
At 298 K, the standard electrode potentials of Cu$^{2+}$ / Cu, Zn$^{2+}$ / Zn, Fe$^{2+}$ / Fe and Ag$^{+}$ / Ag are 0.34 V, –0.76 V, –0.44 V and 0.80 V, respectively.
On the basis of standard electrode potential, predict which of the following reaction cannot occur?
questions.sol:
A metal can displace another from solution only if its reduction potential is lower.
Ag (+0.80 V) has a higher potential than Cu (+0.34 V), so silver cannot reduce Cu$^{2+}$: $E^\circ_{cell} = 0.34 - 0.80 = -0.46$ V. Reaction (4) cannot occur; the others have positive $E^\circ_{cell}$.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements
$\textbf{Statement I:}$
In the coagulation of a negative sol, the flocculating power of the three given ions is in the order
Al$^{3+}$ > Ba$^{2+}$ > Na$^{+}$
$\textbf{Statement II:}$
In the coagulation of a positive sol, the flocculating power of the three given salts is in the order
NaCl > Na$_2$SO$_4$ > Na$_3$PO$_4$
In the light of the above statements, choose the most $\textbf{appropriate}$ answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.sol:
Hardy-Schulze rule: the higher the charge on the oppositely charged ion, the greater its coagulating power.
Statement I is correct for a negative sol (cations). For a positive sol the anions act, so the order is Na₃PO₄ > Na₂SO₄ > NaCl: Statement II is incorrect.

questions.text:
Given below are half cell reactions:
$\text{MnO}_4^- + 8\text{H}^+ + 5\text{e}^- \to \text{Mn}^{2+} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$,
$\text{E}^\circ_{\text{Mn}^{2+}/\text{MnO}_4^-} = -1.510$ V
$\dfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_2 + 2\text{H}^+ + 2\text{e}^- \to \text{H}_2\text{O}$,
$\text{E}^\circ_{\text{O}_2/\text{H}_2\text{O}} = +1.223$ V
Will the permanganate ion, $\text{MnO}_4^-$ liberate $\textbf{O}_\mathbf{2}$ from water in the presence of an acid?
questions.sol:
$E^\circ_{\text{Mn}^{2+}/\text{MnO}_4^-} = -1.510$ V is the oxidation potential, so the reduction potential of MnO$_4^-$/Mn$^{2+}$ is $+1.510$ V.
MnO$_4^-$ is reduced and water is oxidised to O$_2$: $E^\circ_{cell} = 1.510 - 1.223 = +0.287$ V. This is positive, so the reaction is feasible.

What mass of 95% pure CaCO$_3$ will be required to neutralise 50 mL of 0.5 M HCl solution according to the following reaction?

Moles of HCl $= 0.050 \times 0.5 = 0.025$, so moles of CaCO$_3$ $= 0.0125$ and its mass $= 0.0125 \times 100 = 1.25$ g.
Mass of 95% pure sample $= 1.25/0.95 = 1.32$ g.

questions.text: Copper crystallises in fcc unit cell with cell edge length of $3.608 \times 10^{-8}$ cm. The density of copper is 8.92 g cm$^{-3}$. Calculate the atomic mass of copper.

questions.text:
Find the emf of the cell in which the following reaction takes place at 298 K
$\text{Ni(s)} + 2\text{Ag}^+(0.001\,\text{M}) \to \text{Ni}^{2+}(0.001\,\text{M}) + 2\text{Ag(s)}$
$\left(\text{Given that } \text{E}^\circ_{\text{cell}} = 10.5\ \text{V}, \dfrac{2.303\,\text{RT}}{\text{F}} = 0.059 \text{ at } 298\ \text{K}\right)$

Nernst equation with $n = 2$: $E = E^\circ - \dfrac{0.059}{2}\log\dfrac{[\text{Ni}^{2+}]}{[\text{Ag}^+]^2} = E^\circ - 0.0295\log\dfrac{10^{-3}}{10^{-6}} = E^\circ - 0.0885$ V.
With $E^\circ = 10.5$ V as printed, $E = 10.4115$ V, which is not an option. With $E^\circ = 1.05$ V (the value evidently intended), $E = 0.9615$ V, option (3).

questions.note: NTA dropped this question in the final key (code 5 on the key). The printed $E^\circ_{cell} = 10.5$ V gives 10.4115 V, which is not an option; option (3), 0.9615 V, would follow from $E^\circ_{cell} = 1.05$ V.

questions.text: The process of translation of mRNA to proteins begins as soon as :
options: The small subunit of ribosome encounters mRNA
The larger subunit of ribosome encounters mRNA
Both the subunits join together to bind with mRNA
The tRNA is activated and the larger subunit of ribosome encounters mRNA
questions.sol: As NCERT puts it, translation begins when the small subunit of the ribosome encounters the mRNA (with the initiator tRNA). The large subunit joins afterwards.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Match $\textbf{List-I}$ with $\textbf{List-II}$
List-IList-II
(a)Manganese(i)Activates the enzyme catalase
(b)Magnesium(ii)Required for pollen germination
(c)Boron(iii)Activates enzymes of respiration
(d)Iron(iv)Functions in splitting of water during photosynthesis
Choose the $\textbf{correct answer}$ from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Manganese takes part in the splitting of water in photosynthesis; magnesium activates the enzymes of respiration; boron is needed for pollen germination; iron activates catalase.
So (a)-(iv), (b)-(iii), (c)-(ii), (d)-(i).
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Which one of the following never occurs during mitotic cell division?
options: Spindle fibres attach to kinetochores of chromosomes
Movement of centrioles towards opposite poles
Coiling and condensation of the chromatids
questions.sol: Pairing (synapsis) of homologous chromosomes happens only in prophase I of meiosis, never in mitosis.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
$\textbf{Statement I :}$
The primary CO$_2$ acceptor in C$_4$ plants is phosphoenolpyruvate and is found in the mesophyll cells.
$\textbf{Statement II :}$
Mesophyll cells of C$_4$ plants lack RuBisCo enzyme. In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol: Both are correct. PEP in the mesophyll cells is the primary CO₂ acceptor (via PEP carboxylase), and the mesophyll cells of C₄ plants lack RuBisCO, which is confined to the bundle sheath cells.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Which one of the following is $\textbf{not}$ true regarding the release of energy during ATP synthesis through chemiosmosis? It involves:
options: Movement of protons across the membrane to the stroma
Reduction of NADP to NADPH$_2$ on the stroma side of the membrane
questions.sol: In chemiosmosis, ATP is made when the proton gradient breaks down as protons move back through ATP synthase into the stroma. Protons are also used up when NADP is reduced on the stroma side. No 'electron gradient' is involved.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Habitat loss and fragmentation, over exploitation, alien species invasion and co-extinction are causes for:
questions.sol: These are the four main causes of biodiversity loss (the 'Evil Quartet').
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: What is the net gain of ATP when each molecule of glucose is converted to two molecules of pyruvic acid?
questions.sol: Glycolysis uses 2 ATP and produces 4 ATP, a net gain of 2 ATP (plus 2 NADH) per glucose.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: “Girdling Experiment” was performed by Plant Physiologists to identify the plant tissue through which:
options: for both water and food transportation
questions.sol: Removing a ring of bark (with the phloem) makes the bark above the ring swell with accumulated food, while the plant continues to get water through the xylem. This shows that food is carried in the phloem.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Which of the following is $\textbf{not}$ observed during apoplastic pathway ?
options: Movement of water occurs through intercellular spaces and wall of the cells
The movement does not involve crossing of cell membrane
The movement is aided by cytoplasmic streaming
Apoplast is continuous and does not provide any barrier to water movement
questions.sol: The apoplast is the continuous system of cell walls and intercellular spaces, and water moves through it without entering the cytoplasm. Cytoplasmic streaming aids the symplastic pathway, not the apoplastic one.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Which one of the following plants does $\textbf{not}$ show plasticity?
questions.sol: Plasticity (for example heterophylly, different leaf forms at different stages or in different habitats) is shown by cotton, coriander, larkspur and buttercup. Maize does not show it.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: DNA polymorphism forms the basis of :
options: Both genetic mapping and DNA finger printing
questions.sol: As NCERT notes, DNA polymorphism (for example in repetitive DNA) is the basis of genetic mapping of the genome as well as DNA fingerprinting.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: XO type of sex determination can be found in :
questions.sol: In grasshoppers, males have only one X chromosome (XO) and females have XX. Drosophila and monkeys have XY, and birds have ZW.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as $\textbf{Assertion (A)}$ and the other is labelled as $\textbf{Reason (R)}$.
$\textbf{Assertion (A) :}$
Polymerase chain reaction is used in DNA amplification.
$\textbf{Reason (R) :}$
The ampicillin resistant gene is used as a selectable marker to check transformation
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.sol: Both are correct statements, but they are unrelated: PCR amplifies DNA, while an antibiotic resistance gene (ampicillin) is a selectable marker for picking out transformants.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: The gaseous plant growth regulator is used in plants to :
options: promote root growth and roothair formation to increase the absorption surface
kill dicotyledonous weeds in the fields
questions.sol: The gaseous regulator is ethylene, which promotes root growth and root hair formation. Malting uses gibberellin, overcoming apical dominance uses cytokinin, and killing dicot weeds uses the auxin 2,4-D.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: The device which can remove particulate matter present in the exhaust from a thermal power plant is :
questions.sol: An electrostatic precipitator charges dust particles in the exhaust and collects them on plates, removing about 99% of the particulate matter.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
$\textbf{Statement I :}$
Cleistogamous flowers are invariably autogamous
$\textbf{Statement II :}$
Cleistogamy is disadvantageous as there is no chance for cross pollination
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol: Cleistogamous flowers never open, so they can only self-pollinate (invariably autogamous). This assures seed set, but it rules out cross-pollination, which is a disadvantage. Both statements are correct.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Exoskeleton of arthropods is composed of :
questions.sol: The exoskeleton of arthropods is made of chitin, a complex polysaccharide (a polymer of N-acetylglucosamine).
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Read the following statements and choose the set of $\textbf{correct}$ statements :
(a) Euchromatin is loosely packed chromatin
(b) Heterochromatin is transcriptionally active
(c) Histone octomer is wrapped by negatively charged DNA in nucleosome
(d) Histones are rich in lysine and arginine
(e) A typical nucleosome contains 400 bp of DNA helix
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
(a), (c) and (d) are correct.
(b) is wrong: heterochromatin is densely packed and transcriptionally inactive. (e) is wrong: a typical nucleosome has 200 bp of DNA.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Which one of the following statements cannot be connected to Predation?
options: It helps in maintaining species diversity in a community
It might lead to extinction of a species
Both the interacting species are negatively impacted
It is necessitated by nature to maintain the ecological balance
questions.sol: In predation the predator benefits (+) and the prey is harmed (−). Both species being harmed describes competition, not predation.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
The flowers are Zygomorphic in:
(a) Mustard
(b) Gulmohar
(c) $\textit{Cassia}$
(d) $\textit{Datura}$
(e) Chilly
Choose the $\textbf{correct answer}$ from the options given below:
questions.sol: Zygomorphic flowers can be divided into two similar halves in only one plane, as in pea, gulmohar, bean and Cassia. Mustard, Datura and chilli have actinomorphic flowers.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Which one of the following produces nitrogen fixing nodules on the roots of $\textit{Alnus}$?
questions.sol: Frankia, a microbe, forms nitrogen-fixing root nodules on non-leguminous plants such as Alnus. Rhizobium nodulates legumes; Rhodospirillum and Beijerinckia are free-living nitrogen fixers.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Read the following statements about the vascular bundles :
(a) In roots, xylem and phloem in a vascular bundle are arranged in an alternate manner along the different radii.
(b) Conjoint closed vascular bundles do not possess cambium
(c) In open vascular bundles, cambium is present in between xylem and phloem
(d) The vascular bundles of dicotyledonous stem possess endarch protoxylem
(e) In monocotyledonous root, usually there are more than six xylem bundles present
Choose the $\textbf{correct answer}$ from the options given below :
questions.sol:
(b), (c), (d) and (e) are correct: closed bundles lack cambium, open bundles have cambium between xylem and phloem, the dicot stem has endarch protoxylem, and the monocot root is polyarch (usually more than six xylem bundles).
The key treats (a) as wrong: in roots the xylem and phloem form separate radial strands on alternate radii, so they are not 'in a vascular bundle' together.
questions.subject: Botany
questions.note: NTA's final key gives option (2). Statement (a) is close to NCERT's description of radial vascular bundles in roots, and some coaching keys (including Aakash's) said that no option is correct. The key's reading is that xylem and phloem in roots lie in separate strands, not 'in a vascular bundle', so (a) is wrong.

questions.text: Identify the $\textbf{incorrect}$ statement related to Pollination :
options: Pollination by water is quite rare in flowering plants
Pollination by wind is more common amongst abiotic pollination
Flowers produce foul odours to attract flies and beetles to get pollinated
Moths and butterflies are the most dominant pollinating agents among insects
questions.sol: Bees are the dominant insect pollinators, not moths and butterflies. The other three statements are correct.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Which one of the following statement is $\textbf{not true}$ regarding gel electrophoresis technique?
options: The process of extraction of separated DNA strands from gel is called elution.
The separated DNA fragments are stained by using ethidium bromide.
The presence of chromogenic substrate gives blue coloured DNA bands on the gel.
Bright orange coloured bands of DNA can be observed in the gel when exposed to UV light.
questions.sol: DNA in the gel is stained with ethidium bromide and seen as bright orange bands under UV light; cutting out and extracting the bands is elution. A chromogenic substrate (blue colonies) is used in blue-white selection of recombinants, not in gel electrophoresis.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Production of Cucumber has increased manifold in recent years. Application of which of the following phytohormones has resulted in this increased yield as the hormone is known to produce female flowers in the plants :
questions.sol: Ethylene promotes female flowers in cucumbers, which increases the yield of fruit.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: What amount of energy is released from glucose during lactic acid fermentation?
questions.sol: In lactic acid and alcoholic fermentation, less than 7% of the energy in glucose is released, and not all of it is trapped as ATP.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
In old trees the greater part of secondary xylem is dark brown and resistant to insect attack due to :
(a) secretion of secondary metabolities and their deposition in the lumen of vessels.
(b) deposition of organic compounds like tannins and resins in the central layers of stem.
(c) deposition of suberin and aromatic substances in the outer layer of stem.
(d) deposition of tannins, gum, resin and aromatic substances in the peripheral layers of stem.
(e) presence of parenchyma cells, functionally active xylem elements and essential oils.
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: This is heartwood, in the centre of the stem. Its dark colour and resistance come from organic compounds (tannins, resins, oils, gums, aromatic substances) deposited in the central layers, including the lumen of the vessels. So (a) and (b) are correct; the peripheral layers (d) form the sapwood.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: The appearance of recombination nodules on homologous chromosomes during meiosis characterizes :
options: Sites at which crossing over occurs
questions.sol: Recombination nodules appear in pachytene and mark the sites where crossing over takes place between non-sister chromatids.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
$\textbf{Statement I :}$
Mendel studied seven pairs of contrasting traits in pea plants and proposed the Laws of Inheritance.
$\textbf{Statement II :}$
Seven characters examined by Mendel in his experiment on pea plants were seed shape and colour, flower colour, pod shape and colour, flower position and stem height.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol: Both are correct. Mendel's seven characters were seed shape, seed colour, flower colour, pod shape, pod colour, flower position and stem height.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Transposons can be used during which one of the following ?
questions.sol: In RNA interference (gene silencing), the complementary RNA may come from mobile genetic elements (transposons) that replicate through an RNA intermediate.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: While explaining interspecific interaction of population, (+) sign is assigned for beneficial interaction, (–) sign is assigned for detrimental interaction and (0) for neutral interaction. Which of the following interactions can be assigned (+) for one specifies and (–) for another specifies involved in the interaction ?
questions.sol: Predation (like parasitism) is +/−. Amensalism is −/0, commensalism is +/0 and competition is −/−.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Which part of the fruit, labelled in the given figure makes it a false fruit?
questions.sol: The figure is a section of an apple. The fleshy edible part C develops from the thalamus, not the ovary, so it is a false fruit.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Match the plant with the kind of life cycle it exhibits:
List-IList-II
(a)$\textit{Spirogyra}$(i)Dominant diploid sporophyte vascular plant, with highly reduced male or female gametophyte
(b)Fern(ii)Dominant haploid free-living gametophyte
(c)$\textit{Funaria}$(iii)Dominant diploid sporophyte alternating with reduced gametophyte called prothallus
(d)$\textit{Cycas}$(iv)Dominant haploid leafy gametophyte alternating with partially dependent multicellular sporophyte
Choose the $\textbf{correct answer}$ from the options given below :
questions.sol: Spirogyra has a haplontic life cycle with a free-living haploid gametophyte (ii). A fern has a dominant sporophyte and a small prothallus (iii). In the moss Funaria the leafy gametophyte dominates and the sporophyte is partly dependent on it (iv). Cycas is a vascular plant with a dominant sporophyte and much reduced gametophytes (i).
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-IList-II
(a)Metacentric chromosome(i)Centromere situated close to the end forming one extremely short and one very long arms
(b)Acrocentric chromosome(ii)Centromere at the terminal end
(c)Submetacentric(iii)Centromere in the middle forming two equal arms of chromosomes
(d)Telocentric chromosome(iv)Centromere slightly away from the middle forming one shorter arm and one longer arm
Choose the $\textbf{correct answer}$ from the options given below :
questions.sol: Metacentric: centromere in the middle (iii). Acrocentric: close to one end (i). Submetacentric: slightly away from the middle (iv). Telocentric: at the end (ii).
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Addition of more solutes in a given solution will :
options: not affect the water potential at all
questions.sol: Solute potential is always negative, and adding more solute makes it more negative. So the water potential of the solution falls.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Which of the following occurs due to the presence of autosome linked dominant trait ?
questions.sol: Myotonic dystrophy is an autosomal dominant disorder. Sickle cell anaemia and thalassaemia are autosomal recessive, and haemophilia is X-linked recessive.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: Which one of the following will accelerate phosphorus cycle?
questions.sol: Rocks are the natural reservoir of phosphorus, which enters the cycle when the rocks weather and release phosphates into the soil. Faster weathering speeds up the cycle.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: In the following palindromic base sequences of DNA, which one can be cut easily by particular restriction enzyme?
questions.sol: 5′-GAATTC-3′ reads the same on both strands in the 5′→3′ direction (a palindrome) and is the recognition site of EcoRI. The other sequences are not palindromes.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Read the following statements on lipids and find out correct set of statements:
(a) Lecithin found in the plasma membrane is a glycolipid
(b) Saturated fatty acids possess one or more c = c bonds
(c) Gingely oil has lower melting point, hence remains as oil in winter
(d) Lipids are generally insoluble in water but soluble in some organic solvents
(e) When fatty acid is esterified with glycerol, monoglycerides are formed
Choose the correct answer from the option given below:
questions.sol:
(a) is wrong: lecithin is a phospholipid. (b) is wrong: saturated fatty acids have no C=C bonds.
(c), (d) and (e) are correct (one fatty acid esterified with glycerol gives a monoglyceride).
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: What is the role of large bundle sheath cells found around the vascular bundles in C$_4$ plants?
options: To provide the site for photorespiratory pathway
To increase the number of chloroplast for the operation of Calvin cycle
To enable the plant to tolerate high temperature
To protect the vascular tissue from high light intensity
questions.sol: The large bundle sheath cells of C₄ plants (Kranz anatomy) are packed with chloroplasts, and the Calvin cycle runs in them. C₄ plants largely avoid photorespiration.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: If a geneticist uses the blind approach for sequencing the whole genome of an organism, followed by assignment of function to different segments, the methodology adopted by him is called as :
questions.sol: In the Human Genome Project, sequencing the whole genome (coding and non-coding) without bias and then assigning functions to the segments is called sequence annotation. Expressed sequence tags identify only the expressed genes.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as $\textbf{Assertion (A)}$ and the other is labelled as $\textbf{Reason (R)}$.
$\textbf{Assertion (A) :}$ Mendel’s law of Independent assortment does not hold good for the genes that are located closely on the same chromosome.
$\textbf{Reason (R) :}$ Closely located genes assort independently.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.sol: (A) is correct: closely placed genes on one chromosome are linked and tend to be inherited together. (R) is wrong for the same reason: linked genes do not assort independently.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text:
The anatomy of springwood shows some peculiar features. Identify the $\textbf{correct}$ set of statements about springwood.
(a) It is also called as the earlywood
(b) In spring season cambium produces xylem elements with narrow vessels
(c) It is lighter in colour
(d) The springwood along with autumnwood shows alternate concentric rings forming annual rings
(e) It has lower density
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: Springwood (earlywood) is formed when the cambium is very active: it has many xylem elements with wide vessels, so it is lighter in colour and of lower density. With autumnwood it forms the annual rings. Only (b) is wrong.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: The entire fleet of buses in Delhi were converted to CNG from diesel. In reference to this, which one of the following statements is false?
options: CNG burns more efficiently than diesel
The same diesel engine is used in CNG buses making the cost of conversion low
It cannot be adulterated like diesel
questions.sol: CNG burns more efficiently, is cheaper and cannot be adulterated like petrol or diesel. Switching to CNG needed new or modified engines and a network of filling stations, so (2) is false.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.text: $\textit{In-situ}$ conservation refers to:
options: Protect and conserve the whole ecosystem
questions.sol: In situ (on site) conservation protects species in their natural habitat, so the whole ecosystem is protected, as in national parks, sanctuaries and biosphere reserves.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: In which of the following animals, digestive tract has additional chambers like crop and gizzard?
questions.sol: A crop and gizzard are features of the bird digestive tract. Pavo (peacock), Psittacula (parrot) and Corvus (crow) are all birds; each of the other options includes a non-bird.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: If the length of a DNA molecule is 1.1 metres, what will be the approximate number of base pairs?
questions.sol: Adjacent base pairs are 0.34 nm apart: $\dfrac{1.1}{0.34 \times 10^{-9}} \approx 3.2 \times 10^{9}$ bp, i.e. about $3.3 \times 10^{9}$ bp (the size of the human haploid genome).
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
$\textbf{Statement I :}$ Fatty acids and glycerols cannot be absorbed into the blood.
$\textbf{Statement II :}$ Specialized lymphatic capillaries called lacteals carry chylomicrons into lymphatic vessels and ultimately into the blood.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{most appropriate}$ answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol: Both are correct, as in NCERT. Fatty acids and glycerol are insoluble, so they cannot pass straight into the blood. They are taken into micelles, re-formed into fats in the intestinal cells and packed into chylomicrons, which the lacteals carry into the lymph and then the blood.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
$\textbf{Statement I:}$
Autoimmune disorder is a condition where body defense mechanism recognizes its own cells as foreign bodies.
$\textbf{Statement II:}$
Rheumatoid arthritis is a condition where body does not attack self cells.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{most appropriate}$ answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol: Statement I is correct. Statement II is incorrect: rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune disease in which the body attacks its own cells.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text:
Which of the following statements are true for spermatogenesis but do not hold true for Oogenesis?
(a) It results in the formation of haploid gametes
(b) Differentiation of gamete occurs after the completion of meiosis
(c) Meiosis occurs continuously in a mitotically dividing stem cell population
(d) It is controlled by the Luteinising hormone (LH) and Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH) secreted by the anterior pituitary
(e) It is initiated at puberty
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
Only in spermatogenesis do spermatids differentiate into sperms after meiosis is complete (b), does meiosis go on continuously from a self-renewing stem cell population (c), and does the process begin at puberty (e). Oogenesis starts in the foetus.
(a) and (d) are true of both processes.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as $\textbf{Assertion (A)}$ and the other is labelled as $\textbf{Reason (R)}$.
$\textbf{Assertion (A):}$
Osteoporosis is characterised by decreased bone mass and increased chance of fractures.
$\textbf{Reason (R):}$
Common cause of osteoporosis is increased levels of estrogen.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{most appropriate}$ answer from the options given below.
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.sol: (A) is correct. (R) is wrong: a common cause of osteoporosis is a fall in oestrogen levels (for example after menopause), not a rise.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
$\textbf{Statement I:}$
Restriction endonucleases recognise specific sequence to cut DNA known as palindromic nucleotide sequence.
$\textbf{Statement II}$:
Restriction endonucleases cut the DNA strand a little away from the centre of the palindromic site.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{most appropriate}$ answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol: Both are correct. Each restriction endonuclease recognises a specific palindromic sequence and cuts each strand a little away from the centre of the site, between the same two bases, leaving sticky ends.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: Lippe’s loop is a type of contraceptive used as:
questions.sol: The Lippes loop is a non-medicated intra-uterine device. Copper-releasing IUDs include CuT, Cu7 and Multiload 375.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: Under normal physiological conditions in human being every 100 ml of oxygenated blood can deliver ________ ml of O$_2$ to the tissues.
questions.sol: Every 100 ml of oxygenated blood delivers about 5 ml of O₂ to the tissues under normal conditions.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
$\textbf{Assertion (A) :}$ All vertebrates are chordates but all chordates are not vertebrates.
$\textbf{Reason (R) :}$ Notochord is replaced by vertebral column in the adult vertebrates.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{most appropriate}$ answer from the option given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.sol: Both are correct, and (R) explains (A): vertebrates have a notochord in the embryo that is replaced by a vertebral column in the adult. Chordates such as urochordates and cephalochordates keep the notochord without forming a vertebral column, so they are not vertebrates.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: Which of the following is $\textbf{not}$ a connective tissue?
questions.sol: Neuroglia are supporting cells of neural tissue. Blood, adipose tissue and cartilage are connective tissues.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: Nitrogenous waste is excreted in the form of pellet or paste by :
questions.sol: Birds such as Pavo (peacock) are uricotelic and excrete uric acid as a pellet or paste with very little water.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: Regarding Meiosis, which of the statements is $\textbf{incorrect}$?
options: There are two stages in Meiosis, Meiosis-I and II
DNA replication occurs in S phase of Meiosis-II
Pairing of homologous chromosomes and recombination occurs in Meiosis-I
Four haploid cells are formed at the end of Meiosis-II
questions.sol: DNA replicates only once, in the S phase of the interphase before meiosis I. There is no S phase before meiosis II, so statement (2) is incorrect.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: In an $\textit{E. Coli}$ strain $\textit{i}$ gene gets mutated and its product can not bind the inducer molecule. If growth medium is provided with lactose, what will be the outcome?
options: $\textit{z, y, a}$ genes will be transcribed
$\textit{z, y, a}$ genes will not be translated
RNA polymerase will bind the promoter region
questions.sol: The i gene codes for the repressor. If the repressor cannot bind the inducer (allolactose), it stays bound to the operator even when lactose is present. RNA polymerase is blocked, so the z, y and a genes are not transcribed and hence not translated.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: Which of the following is a correct match for disease and its symptoms?
options: Tetany – High Ca$^{2+}$ level causing rapid spasms.
Myasthenia gravis – Genetic disorder resulting in weakening and paralysis of skeletal muscle
Muscular dystrophy – An auto immune disorder causing progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle
questions.sol: Arthritis is inflammation of the joints. Tetany is caused by low Ca²⁺, myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder, and muscular dystrophy is a genetic disorder.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: Identify the microorganism which is responsible for the production of an immunosuppressive molecule cyclosporin A :
questions.sol: Cyclosporin A, used as an immunosuppressant in organ transplant patients, is produced by the fungus Trichoderma polysporum.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : Mycoplasma can pass through less than 1 micron filter size.
Statement II : Mycoplasma are bacteria with cell wall.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol: Statement I is correct: mycoplasmas are the smallest living cells (about 0.1 µm) and pass through bacterial filters. Statement II is incorrect: mycoplasmas completely lack a cell wall.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: Which of the following functions is $\textbf{not}$ performed by secretions from salivary glands?
questions.sol: Saliva lubricates the mouth (mucus), controls bacteria (lysozyme) and starts digesting starch into the disaccharide maltose (salivary amylase). It does not digest disaccharides; that happens in the small intestine.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
$\textbf{Statement I :}$ The coagulum is formed of network of threads called thrombins.
$\textbf{Statement II :}$ Spleen is the graveyard of erythrocytes.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{most appropriate}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol: Statement I is incorrect: the clot is a network of threads called fibrins (thrombin is the enzyme that forms them). Statement II is correct: the spleen destroys old red blood cells.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: A dehydration reaction links two glucose molecules to product maltose. If the formula for glucose is C$_6$H$_{12}$O$_6$ then what is the formula for maltose?
questions.sol: Two glucose molecules lose one molecule of water: 2 C₆H₁₂O₆ − H₂O = C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: Which of the following statements with respect to Endoplasmic Reticulum is incorrect?
options: RER has ribosomes attached to ER
In prokaryotes only RER are present
SER are the sites for lipid synthesis
questions.sol: Prokaryotes have no membrane-bound organelles, so they have no endoplasmic reticulum at all. Statement (3) is incorrect.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: Which of the following is present between the adjacent bones of the vertebral column?
questions.sol: Cartilage (the intervertebral discs) lies between adjacent vertebrae. Intercalated discs are junctions between cardiac muscle cells.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: Tegmina in cockroach, arises from
questions.sol: The first pair of wings (tegmina, the leathery forewings) arises from the mesothorax; the second pair arises from the metathorax.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
$\textbf{Statement I :}$
The release of sperms into the seminiferous tubules is called spermiation.
$\textbf{Statement II :}$
Spermiogenesis is the process of formation of sperms from spermatogonia.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{most appropriate}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol: Statement I is correct. Statement II is incorrect: spermiogenesis is the change of spermatids into sperms; forming sperms from spermatogonia is spermatogenesis.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: If ‘8’ $\textit{Drosophila}$ in a laboratory population of ‘80’ died during a week, the death rate in the population is ______ individuals per $\textit{Drosophila}$ per week.
questions.sol: Death rate = deaths ÷ population = 8/80 = 0.1 individuals per Drosophila per week.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: Natural selection where more individuals acquire specific character value other than the mean character value, leads to
questions.sol: When selection favours a value on one side of the mean, the population mean shifts in that direction: directional change. Stabilising selection favours the mean, and disruptive selection favours both extremes.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: Which of the following is not the function of conducting part of respiratory system?
options: It clears inhaled air from foreign particles
Temperature of inhaled air is brought to body temperature
Provides surface for diffusion of O$_2$ and CO$_2$
questions.sol: The conducting part (nose to terminal bronchioles) carries air to the alveoli and cleans, humidifies and warms it. Gas exchange by diffusion takes place in the respiratory (exchange) part, the alveoli.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: Breeding crops with higher levels of vitamins and minerals or higher proteins and healthier fats is called :
questions.sol: Biofortification is breeding crops with more vitamins, minerals, protein or healthier fats to improve public health.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: In the taxonomic categories which hierarchical arrangement in ascending order is $\textbf{correct}$ in case of animals?
options: Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species
Kingdom, Class, Phylum, Family, Order, Genus, Species
Kingdom, Order, Class, Phylum, Family, Genus, Species
Kingdom, Order, Phylum, Class, Family, Genus, Species
questions.sol: The correct sequence for animals is Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species. Only option (1) has the categories in the right order. Strictly, this order runs from the highest rank down, i.e. descending; ascending would be Species to Kingdom.
questions.subject: Zoology
questions.note: Option (1) lists the categories from the highest rank (Kingdom) down to Species, which is descending, not ascending, order. None of the options gives an ascending order. NTA's final key gives option (1), the only correct sequence.

questions.text: At which stage of life the oogenesis process is initiated?
questions.sol: Oogenesis starts during embryonic (foetal) development, when oogonia form and enter meiosis I as primary oocytes. These stay arrested until puberty.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: Identify the asexual reproductive structure associated with $\textit{Penicillium}$ :
questions.sol: Penicillium (an ascomycete) reproduces asexually by conidia, spores formed at the tips of conidiophores.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: In gene therapy of Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency, the patient requires periodic infusion of genetically engineered lymphocytes because :
options: Retroviral vector is introduced into these lymphocytes.
Gene isolated from marrow cells producing ADA is introduced into cells at embryonic stages
Lymphocytes from patient's blood are grown in culture, outside the body.
Genetically engineered lymphocytes are not immortal cells.
questions.sol: The lymphocytes given the functional ADA gene are not immortal; they die after a time, so the treatment has to be repeated periodically.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: Select the $\textbf{incorrect}$ statement with reference to mitosis:
options: All the chromosomes lie at the equator at metaphase
Spindle fibres attach to centromere of chromosomes
Splitting of centromere occurs at anaphase
questions.sol: Spindle fibres attach to the kinetochores, small disc-shaped structures on the centromere, not to the centromere itself. The key treats (2) as the incorrect statement; the other three are standard facts about mitosis.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: Detritivores breakdown detritus into smaller particles. This process is called:
questions.sol: Fragmentation is the breakdown of detritus into smaller particles by detritivores such as earthworms. It is the first step of decomposition.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: If a colour blind female marries a man whose mother was also colour blind, what are the chances of her progeny having colour blindness?
questions.sol:
The woman is X$^c$X$^c$. The man got his X from his colour-blind mother, so he is X$^c$Y.
Every daughter is X$^c$X$^c$ and every son X$^c$Y: all the children are colour blind (100%).
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: Select the $\textbf{incorrect}$ statement with respect to acquired immunity.
options: Primary response is produced when our body encounters a pathogen for the first time.
Anamnestic response is elicited on subsequent encounters with the same pathogen.
Anamnestic response is due to memory of first encounter.
Acquired immunity is non-specific type of defense present at the time of birth.
questions.sol: Acquired immunity is pathogen-specific and develops during life. Innate immunity is the non-specific defence present at birth.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text:
Statements related to human Insulin are given below.
Which statement(s) is/are $\textbf{correct}$ about genetically engineered Insulin?
(a) Pro-hormone insulin contain extra stretch of C-peptide
(b) A-peptide and B-peptide chains of insulin were produced separately in $\textit{E.coli}$, extracted and combined by creating disulphide bond between them.
(c) Insulin used for treating Diabetes was extracted from Cattles and Pigs.
(d) Pro-hormone Insulin needs to be processed for converting into a mature and functional hormone.
(e) Some patients develop allergic reactions to the foreign insulin.
Choose $\textbf{the most appropriate}$ answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
Only (b) describes genetically engineered insulin: Eli Lilly made the A and B chains separately in E. coli and joined them with disulphide bonds, so no pro-hormone is involved.
(a) and (d) describe natural pro-insulin, and (c) and (e) describe the older insulin taken from cattle and pigs.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: Which one of the following statements is $\textbf{correct}$?
options: The atrio-ventricular node (AVN) generates an action potential to stimulate atrial contraction
The tricuspid and the bicuspid valves open due to the pressure exerted by the simultaneous contraction of the atria
Blood moves freely from atrium to the ventricle during joint diastole.
Increased ventricular pressure causes closing of the semilunar valves.
questions.sol:
During joint diastole the AV valves are open and blood flows freely from the atria into the ventricles (about 70% of ventricular filling).
The SAN, not the AVN, starts atrial contraction; the AV valves are already open before atrial systole; and the semilunar valves close when ventricular pressure falls.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text:
Match $\textbf{List-I}$ with $\textbf{List-II}$
List-I
(Biological Molecules)		List-II
(Biological functions)
(a)Glycogen(i)Hormone
(b)Globulin(ii)Biocatalyst
(c)Steroids(iii)Antibody
(d)Thrombin(iv)Storage product
Choose the $\textbf{correct answer}$ from the options given below:
questions.sol:
Glycogen is a storage product; globulins (immunoglobulins) are antibodies; many hormones are steroids; thrombin is an enzyme (biocatalyst).
So (a)-(iv), (b)-(iii), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii).
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: Ten $\textit{E.coli}$ cells with $^{15}$N - dsDNA are incubated in medium containing $^{14}$N nucleotide. After 60 minutes, how many $\textit{E.coli}$ cells will have DNA totally free from $^{15}$N?
questions.sol:
E. coli divides every 20 minutes, so 60 minutes gives 3 generations: $10 \to 80$ cells.
Replication is semi-conservative, so the two $^{15}$N strands of each original DNA end up in 2 cells: $10 \times 2 = 20$ hybrid cells.
Cells with DNA free of $^{15}$N $= 80 - 20 = 60$.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: The recombination frequency between the genes a & c is 5%, b & c is 15%, b & d is 9%, a & b is 20%, c & d is 24% and a & d is 29%. What will be the sequence of these genes on a linear chromosome?
questions.sol:
Map distances add up along the chromosome: a–c 5 + c–b 15 = a–b 20; c–b 15 + b–d 9 = c–d 24; a–c 5 + c–b 15 + b–d 9 = a–d 29.
So the order is a, c, b, d.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text:
Which of the following are $\textbf{not}$ the effects of Parathyroid hormone?
(a) Stimulates the process of bone resorption
(b) Decreases Ca$^{2+}$ level in blood
(c) Reabsorption of Ca$^{2+}$ by renal tubules
(d) Decreases the absorption of Ca$^{2+}$ from digested food
(e) Increases metabolism of carbohydrates
Choose the $\textbf{most appropriate}$ answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
Parathyroid hormone raises blood Ca²⁺: it stimulates bone resorption (a), reabsorption of Ca²⁺ by the renal tubules (c) and absorption of Ca²⁺ from digested food.
So (b), (d) and (e) are not its effects.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: Which of the following is $\textbf{not}$ a desirable feature of a cloning vector?
options: Presence of single restriction enzyme site
Presence of two or more recognition sites
questions.sol: A cloning vector should have a single recognition site for a given restriction enzyme. Two or more sites would cut the vector into several fragments and complicate cloning.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: Which of the following statements $\textbf{is not}$ true?
options: Analogous structures are a result of convergent evolution
Sweet potato and potato is an example of analogy
Flippers of penguins and dolphins are a pair of homologous organs
questions.sol: The flippers of penguins and dolphins do the same job but evolved separately: they are analogous organs, an example of convergent evolution. So statement (4) is not true.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: Select the $\textbf{incorrect}$ statement regarding synapses :
options: The membranes of presynaptic and postsynaptic neurons are in close proximity in an electrical synapse.
Electrical current can flow directly from one neuron into the other across the electrical synapse.
Impulse transmission across a chemical synapse is always faster than that across an electrical synapse.
questions.sol: Transmission across an electrical synapse is faster than across a chemical synapse, which has to release and detect a neurotransmitter. Statement (4) is incorrect.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text:
Match $\textbf{List-I}$ with $\textbf{List-II}$
List-IList-II
(a)Bronchioles(i)Dense Regular Connective Tissue
(b)Goblet Cell(ii)Loose Connective Tissue
(c)Tendons(iii)Glandular Tissue
(d)Adipose Tissue(iv)Ciliated Epithelium
Choose the $\textbf{correct answer}$ from the options given below:
questions.sol:
Bronchioles are lined by ciliated epithelium; a goblet cell is a unicellular gland (glandular tissue); tendons are dense regular connective tissue; adipose tissue is a loose connective tissue.
So (a)-(iv), (b)-(iii), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii).
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text:
Match $\textbf{List-I}$ with $\textbf{List-II}$ with respect to methods of Contraception and their respective actions.
List-IList-II
(a)Diaphragms(i)Inhibit ovulation and Implantation
(b)Contraceptive Pills(ii)Increase phagocytosis of sperm within Uterus
(c)Intra Uterine Devices(iii)Absence of Menstrual cycle and ovulation following parturition
(d)Lactational Amenorrhea(iv)They cover the cervix blocking the entry of sperms
Choose the $\textbf{correct answer}$ from the options given below:
questions.sol:
Diaphragms cover the cervix; pills inhibit ovulation and implantation; IUDs increase phagocytosis of sperms in the uterus; lactational amenorrhoea is the absence of menstruation and ovulation after childbirth.
So (a)-(iv), (b)-(i), (c)-(ii), (d)-(iii).
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text: Which of the following is a $\textbf{correct}$ statement?
options: Cyanobacteria are a group of autotrophic organisms classified under kingdom Monera.
Slime moulds are saprophytic organisms classified under Kingdom Monera.
Mycoplasma have DNA, ribosome and cell wall.
questions.sol: Cyanobacteria are photosynthetic autotrophs in Monera. Some bacteria are autotrophs, slime moulds are in Protista and mycoplasmas have no cell wall.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
$\textbf{Statements I :}$
In a scrubber the exhaust from the thermal plant is passed through the electric wires to charge the dust particles.
$\textbf{Statement II :}$
Particulate matter (PM 2.5) cannot be removed by scrubber but can be removed by an electrostatic precipitator.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{most appropriate}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol: Statement I is incorrect: charging dust particles with electrode wires is how an electrostatic precipitator works; a scrubber sprays water or lime to remove gases such as SO₂. Statement II is correct as the key treats it: fine particulate matter is removed by an electrostatic precipitator, not by a scrubber.
questions.subject: Zoology
